Each of the two topics follows the full Spec 008 per-topic learning cycle: a real classroom situation opens the topic, an Explanation with definitions and worked examples follows, a group activity (mapping institutions; tracing one event across institutions) asks learners to apply, Check your understanding questions (four per topic, Bloom-labelled) provide retrieval practice, a Summary consolidates, a Self-assessment checklist (five items) lets learners self-monitor, a practicum-school task grounds the learning in the trainee's own school, and a Summative task with a mini-rubric requires higher-order writing.
Activities are feasible in a Pakistani/Sindhi classroom context (group work on known communities, pairs tracing a flood scenario, no special materials required).

Progression across topics is deliberate: Topic 5.1 establishes the definition of an institution and the idea of interdependence; Topic 5.2 extends to three more institutions and introduces institutional change. The index.mdx 'How to use this unit' advises reading 5.1 first because 5.2 builds on it.
Retrieval practice is embedded: each topic's summative task returns to the opening vignette (Sana in 5.1, Kotri mill in 5.2), and the unit-assessment ERQs require cross-topic institutional thinking.
The unit-teacher-notes.mdx provides guidance on sequencing (Weeks 11-12), handling the three most common misconceptions, and pacing - supporting actual classroom delivery.

findings.message: OpenStax section 15.1 (Religion) was opened by the authoring team but its wording was not extracted, so the religion subsection's source support relies on a conerly2021 section that was read only at a general level plus Durkheim carried from Unit 1. The religion claims themselves (meaning, moral guidance, cohesion/identity, life-course rituals, sociology studies what religion does without judging belief) are well-established sociological common ground, but a section 15.1 excerpt would strengthen the sources file.

The three no-external-source items in sources/unit-05.md (Lady Health Worker programme started 1994, spread of low-fee private schooling, Council of Islamic Ideology advisory role) are general Pakistani knowledge without a bound source. They are stated in general terms, which is honest, but a reviewer with access to a confirming source (e.g., a government health document for the 1994 date, Constitution of Pakistan Article 230 for the Council) could tighten them.

Render inspection (visual accessibility: small-screen layout at 360px, table scrollability, A4 print views, figure clipping) cannot be performed. The crew job constraint prohibits running npm run build, a dev server, or Playwright, all of which are required to produce a rendered page for inspection. Structural accessibility checks (alt text, heading hierarchy, link text, SVG role/title/desc, figure text measurement) all pass from source, but a render-review requires a live build. This is a tooling limitation, not a content defect. A separate render inspection is required before this unit can be certified at G3.
